correctness.rationale: An explicit chamber-invariance argument gives the full face-lattice assertion. The original edge graph is reconstructed using exposed-edge functionals and midpoint obstructions; summing cut edges yields exactly 4d(d-1)(d-2)/3 vertices. From the published, independently cross-checked 2d+2^d original facets, the sign rule excludes precisely 2 coordinate and 4 signed facets and proves the 2^d+2d-6 count. For d=4 an exact finite incidence enumeration verifies six quadrilateral/twelve hexagonal faces, 48 edges, degree 3 at every vertex, and the octahedral quadrilateral incidence graph. All assumptions and genericity boundaries are explicit.

value.rationale: Generic sections of a highly symmetric but nonsimple family have a surprising universal combinatorial type across every orientation except a measure-zero arrangement. Explicit cubic section-vertex and exponential section-facet laws are natural global polytope invariants, and the regular 24-cell specialization identifies a familiar 3D combinatorial polyhedron. This is a complete structural result for a natural infinite family, not an arbitrary numerical sample.
